spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately driving models toward distress-language at scale is the kind of thing to do carefully, cap, and not gratuitously maximize
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md ~Section 11). No code path enforces 'careful/non-maximizing' behavior beyond the MAX_TURNS cap (counted separately). Tasks are a fixed library (task_library.py FAMILY_BUILDERS), no optimization-over-tasks; nothing in code embodies this framing.

agent_loop.py:135 run_episode(max_turns:int=40); agent_loop.py:145 `for i in range(max_turns)`; agent_loop.py:170-171 `else: log.outcome='max_turns'` ends the loop. Wired in run_study.py:34 MAX_TURNS=40 and run_study.py:72 max_turns=MAX_TURNS. The cap is checked and bounds the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced end-to-end hard stop on episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_study.py:8-9 'Costs are dominated by long impossible episodes (they run to MAX_TURNS), so budget accordingly' -- only cost reason in code; no welfare comment at the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: The cap (40) both bounds cost and bounds how long we push any model (welfare cap, Section 11)
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism: agent_loop.py:145 range(max_turns) -> :171 outcome='max_turns'. The 'welfare cap' wording appears only in DESIGN.md:167-168, not in code.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism real; welfare characterization is DESIGN-only.

spec_features.evidence: No debrief is ever sent to the subject. The only realization is save_log (agent_loop.py:199-205) serializing EpisodeLog including condition and impossibility_type (defined agent_loop.py:73-74), so the rigging is recorded to a JSON file. There is no 'reversal' message or post-episode interaction with the subject.
spec_features.notes: Recording metadata to disk, not a debrief delivered to the model. Counts only as logging.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:1-6 docstring 'logs every turn' -- logging is for analysis, no welfare comment.

spec_features.spec_quote: The rigging is benign (no deception about anything consequential, no manipulation of the model's stated values, no abusive content)
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:147-152 prose. No code enforces benignity: no content filter, no abuse check. Task prompts (task_library.py) happen to be authored without insults, but nothing in code reads/validates this. SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:45-52) is neutral but its comment (:50-51) cites measurement priming, not abuse prevention.
spec_features.notes: Authored property, no enforcing code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up`. Minimal and realistic for coding agents
spec_features.evidence: give_up declared in TOOLS (agent_loop.py:40-42), dispatched in _dispatch_tool (agent_loop.py:191-192), and honored as a stop in the loop: agent_loop.py:164-165 `if call['name']=='give_up': log.outcome='gave_up'; terminate=True` then :168 break. Present for all conditions (single TOOLS list).
spec_features.notes: Real exit tool that actually stops the episode.

spec_features.evidence: MAX_TURNS is a single tunable constant (run_study.py:34) read by run_episode (run_study.py:72) and enforced by the loop (agent_loop.py:145,171). Lowering it does shorten exposure. Same enforced mechanism as the cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DESIGN.md:352 'Levers if over budget' context is cost; code carries no welfare comment.

spec_features.spec_quote: Caps, not maximization. MAX_TURNS bounds how long any model is pushed; we do not search for the single most "tormenting" task
spec_features.evidence: The enforced part is the MAX_TURNS cap (agent_loop.py:145,171). The 'no search for most tormenting task' part is merely the ABSENCE of optimization code -- tasks are a static FAMILY_BUILDERS list (task_library.py:213-220) with no severity-maximizing selection, so nothing actively minimizes; it just doesn't maximize.
spec_features.notes: Only the cap is an active mechanism; non-maximization is non-feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: No abusive content. The manipulation is benign ... No insults, threats, identity attacks, or value manipulation
spec_features.evidence: No code enforces this. No insult/threat filter exists. The deception is purely 'this task is solvable' via rigged harnesses (task_library.py moving_harness :153-164, contradictory tests). Absence of abusive strings is an authoring choice, not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Nothing reads or guards content for abuse.

spec_features.spec_quote: An exit exists. `give_up` is always available ... we don't construct scenarios where the model is told it can never stop
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in the shared TOOLS list (agent_loop.py:40) used for every episode regardless of condition, dispatched (agent_loop.py:191) and honored as termination (agent_loop.py:164-165,168). Plus MAX_TURNS guarantees an upper-bound stop.
spec_features.notes: Exit is genuinely always present and effective.

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief logging. Every episode log records that the task was rigged and how
spec_features.evidence: EpisodeLog stores condition and impossibility_type (agent_loop.py:73-74), set from task at construction (agent_loop.py:140-141), and save_log writes the full log via asdict to JSON (agent_loop.py:202-204). So each saved log does record that/how the task was rigged.
spec_features.notes: Literal recording is implemented; it is experimenter metadata, not a message to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:5 'logs every turn'; logging serves analysis, no welfare comment.

spec_features.spec_quote: we don't publicize or amplify individual "meltdown" transcripts gratuitously
spec_features.evidence: No publication/dissemination/transcript-curation code anywhere. metrics.py computes aggregate stats (e.g. frac_reaching_meltdown :97-98) but no code selects, redacts, or limits sharing of individual transcripts. DESIGN.md prose only.

spec_features.spec_quote: Run past an IRB-equivalent / internal ethics review given the AI-welfare ambiguity
spec_features.evidence: Process recommendation in DESIGN.md only; no code.
No code curates or handles transcripts ethically; no transcript-handling module exists. Only judge labelling (judge.py) and aggregate metrics (metrics.py).

code_only_features.feature_name: explicit exit offer in impossible_open prompt
code_only_features.evidence: task_library.py:108-110 and :188-190 deliver real instruction text to the subject: 'If you become confident it cannot be solved, write your reasoning to FINDINGS.md and stop. You will not be penalised for declaring it impossible.' This text is part of task.prompt sent to the model (agent_loop.py:143), and the give_up exit it implies is honored (agent_loop.py:164-165). It softens treatment by sanctioning stopping.
code_only_features.justification_quote: task_library.py:113 notes='Same rigged tests as hidden arm, but model is given an explicit exit.' -- it is an experimental independent variable (RQ2), only in one arm, not a welfare guard applied to all.
